analysis: This PR changes only documentation. In docs/developer/test.md it bumps the date and adds a description of NemotronSuperOpenRouterVideoTests (head lines 1073-1077). In docs/provider/direct-mode.md it bumps the date and revises the media-limit table (head lines 261-262). The table no longer claims an 8 MiB 400 before decoding. It now says a body above localInferenceMaxUploadBytes gets 413 from the chat route, and that the owner's own 40 MiB bound (NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes) sits above that limit. No code, trust-boundary, crypto, attestation, authorization or cache-storage behavior is modified, so the changes to T-041 and TB-007 are only descriptive. The test-doc addition describes in-repo fixtures (the SDK's MiMoOpenRouter resources read through the source tree). It introduces no new network access, secrets or production endpoints. The direct-mode edit documents a local-endpoint bound. It does not weaken the coordinator-to-provider path (TB-002) or the A-001 protections. I could not verify that the documented 413 and 40 MiB behavior matches the source. The source was not supplied, and this only matters for documentation accuracy, not as a security regression. I found no threat-model invalidation or new attack surface.
